benefits.titleEn: It Compresses a Longer Recovery Process
benefits.en: After the defeat, the players went somewhere quiet to lick their wounds.

benefits.titleEn: It Connects a Setback with a Period of Recovery
benefits.titleZh: 把挫折與休整期連繫起來
benefits.en: 1. something disappointing happened; 2. the person or group now needs time to recover.
benefits.zh: 這個表達同時帶出兩個概念：先發生挫折，之後需要休整。

benefits.titleEn: It Can Describe Individuals and Groups
benefits.en: It Can Describe Individuals and Groups

examples.en: Give her time to lick her wounds.

origin.statusEn: Gradual Metaphorical Development; Exact First Use Uncertain
origin.statusZh: 逐漸形成的比喻用法；確切首次用法不明

history.en: Related wording involving licking oneself clean or whole has been traced by reference works to the sixteenth century, although the precise first use of the modern expression is uncertain. John Dryden’s 1677 play All for Love contains an early figurative example in which defeated forces withdraw and lick their wounds. This shows that the image was already being used metaphorically in the seventeenth century, but it does not prove who first created the expression.
history.zh: 有參考資料把較早期的相關說法追溯至十六世紀，但現代形式的確切首次用法仍未能確認。 John Dryden 在1677年的劇作《All for Love》中，已使用「敗方退下來舔舐傷口」的比喻畫面。 這證明相關比喻在十七世紀已經出現，但不能證明是誰最先創造這個表達。

history.en: A wounded animal temporarily withdraws and attends to its injuries. Speakers extended this physical image to people, teams and organisations recovering emotionally or practically after defeat, embarrassment, rejection or failure.
history.zh: 受傷動物會暫時退下來處理傷處。 後來，人們把這個身體畫面延伸至個人、球隊或組織在落敗、 尷尬、被拒或失敗後休整。

origin.memoryEn: The animal withdraws to recover from an injury; the person withdraws to recover from a setback.
origin.memoryZh: 動物退下來養傷；人則退下來平復挫敗。

rules.titleZh: 規則一：所有格必須配合主語
規則二：wounds 必須使用複數
rules.en: The singular form may describe a real injury, but it is not the standard form of this idiom.
rules.zh: 單數形式可能描述真正的傷口，但不是這個慣用語的標準形式。

rules.titleZh: 規則三：lick 按一般規則變化
規則四：必須先有挫折或負面經歷
rules.en: The context must contain a genuine setback.
rules.zh: 語境必須包含真正的失敗、落敗、拒絕或令人難受的經歷。

rules.titleEn: Do Not Use It for an Ordinary Rest
rules.titleZh: 規則五：不要用來表示一般休息
rules.en: The speaker is merely tired. No defeat or upsetting experience has occurred.
rules.zh: 說話者只是疲倦，並沒有經歷失敗或打擊。 我的建議被拒，因此我會回家休整一下。

examples.en: My proposal was rejected, so I am going home to lick my wounds.
examples.zh: 我的建議被拒，因此我會回家休整一下。

rules.titleEn: Do Not Confuse It with Physical Treatment
rules.titleZh: 規則六：不要與真正的傷口處理混淆
rules.en: The injured dog licked its wound.
rules.zh: 受傷的狗舔自己的傷口。 落敗的球隊回家休整。

examples.en: The defeated team went home to lick its wounds.
examples.zh: 落敗的球隊回家休整。

rules.titleZh: 規則七：保留時態及確定程度
規則八：保留造成打擊的事件
rules.en: When the answer must stand alone, the setback should normally remain visible.
rules.zh: 當答案需要獨立理解時，通常應保留造成打擊的事件。

rules.titleEn: Do Not Repeat the Idiom’s Meaning
rules.titleZh: 規則九：不要再次解釋相同意思
rules.en: The source explains the recovery. The idiom replaces that explanation.
rules.zh: 原句負責解釋「恢復」； 答案則以慣用語濃縮這個意思，不應再次重複。

rules.titleZh: 規則十：嚴重情況下要小心使用
rules.en: In sensitive contexts, recover, grieve, receive support or take time to heal may be more appropriate.
rules.zh: 在涉及死亡、嚴重創傷、重病或重大個人危機時，這個慣用語可能顯得過於輕率。

rules.titleEn: “Still Licking Your Wounds” May Sound Critical
rules.en: “Still Licking Your Wounds” May Sound Critical
rules.zh: still licking your wounds 可能帶有批評意味她正在花幾天時間休整。 幾個月後，她仍在為那次挫敗而自怨自艾。

examples.en: She is taking a few days to lick her wounds.
examples.zh: 她正在花幾天時間休整。

examples.en: She is still licking her wounds months later.
examples.zh: 幾個月後，她仍在為那次挫敗而自怨自艾。

rules.titleEn: Do Not Use “One’s” in a Normal Personal
rules.titleZh: 規則十二：一般句子中不要直接使用 one’s
rules.en: Do Not Use “One’s” in a Normal Personal
rules.zh: 一般句子中不要直接使用 one’s
